question:
Let \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) \(d,\) and \(e\) be distinct integers such that

\[ \begin{aligned} &(6-a)(6-b)(6-c) \\ &\quad {}\cdot(6-d)(6-e) \\ &=45. \end{aligned} \]

What is \(a+b+c+d+e?\)
solution:
Work with the five factors \(6-a,6-b,6-c,6-d,6-e\). They are distinct nonzero integers, and their product is the odd number \(45\), so every factor is odd.

An odd factor has absolute value \(1\) or at least \(3\). Distinctness allows at most two factors of absolute value \(1\), namely \(1\) and \(-1\). If either were missing, at least four factors would have absolute value at least \(3\), making the absolute product at least
\[
3^4=81>45.
\]
Therefore both \(1\) and \(-1\) must occur.

The other three factors have absolute values greater than \(1\), with product \(45=3\cdot3\cdot5\). Each must use at least one of these three prime factors, so their absolute values are \(3,3,5\). Distinctness forces the two factors of absolute value \(3\) to be \(3\) and \(-3\). The four factors \(1,-1,3,-3\) have product \(9\), so the final factor must be \(5\).

Thus the factor set is \(\{-3,-1,1,3,5\}\), which is distinct and does have product \(45\). Its sum is \(5\). Consequently,
\[
a+b+c+d+e=5\cdot6-5=\boxed{25},
\]
choice C.
